name: num
title: Format a numeric vector in a tibble

origin.description: Mark a numeric vector as pillar_num and store how its column should be formatted.
origin.usage: num(x, ..., sigfig = NULL, digits = NULL, label = NULL, scale = NULL, notation = c("fit", "dec", "sci", "eng", "si"), fixed_exponent = NULL, extra_sigfig = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector. An integer is stored as double. A string or a logical value is rejected.

arguments.name: sigfig, digits
arguments.text: Significant figures, or digits after the decimal point. digits must be a whole number. A negative digits value counts significant digits on the other side of the decimal.

arguments.name: label, scale
arguments.text: A label printed with the type, and a scale that requires that label.

arguments.name: notation
arguments.text: fit, dec, sci, eng, or si. Omitted, it stays unset. The installed match is exact.

arguments.name: fixed_exponent, extra_sigfig
arguments.text: An exponent kept in the type, and a flag that asks for one extra significant figure. extra_sigfig cannot be combined with digits.

origin.details: The pillar attribute formats as pillar_num, or pillar_num(notation) when notation is set. digits >= 0 appends :.<digits>! and digits < 0 appends :.<abs(digits)> with no bang. Otherwise sigfig appends :<sigfig>, and a trailing * when extra_sigfig is TRUE. extra_sigfig TRUE on its own appends *. A label appends {label}, a scale appends *<scale>, and a fixed exponent appends |<exponent>. vec_ptype_full returns that string. The abbreviation uses notation, or num, then digits or sigfig. It ignores the label, the scale, and the exponent. digits > 0 keeps the bang in the abbreviation, so zero is :.0 with no bang. A decimal notation with a fixed exponent that is not zero stops with the installed spelling Incomatible. Zero does not, because the test is &&.
origin.value: A double vector of class pillar_num. The data and the formatted pillar attribute are the check. The column printer is separate.
origin.example:
show_num <- function(x) {
  cat(paste(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", format(as.vector(x), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(format(attr(x, "pillar", exact = TRUE)), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr(x), "\n", sep = "")
}

show_num(num(c(1, 2.5, NA)))
cat("\n")
show_num(num(c(1, 2), sigfig = 4, label = "kg"))
cat("\n")
show_num(num(1, digits = 2, notation = "sci"))
cat("\n")
show_num(num(1, notation = "si", fixed_exponent = -3, scale = 10, label = "m"))

translation.description: The same attribute. None is a missing number. A bool is not numeric. An int becomes a float.
translation.usage: num(x, sigfig=None, digits=None, label=None, scale=None, notation=None, fixed_exponent=None, extra_sigfig=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A number, or a list of numbers. None is missing. A bool or a string is rejected. A scalar is a length-1 vector.

arguments.name: sigfig, digits
arguments.text: Significant figures, or digits after the decimal point. digits must be integerish. A negative digits value is written without the bang.

arguments.name: label, scale
arguments.text: A label printed with the type. scale without a label is an error.

arguments.name: notation
arguments.text: "fit", "dec", "sci", "eng", or "si", or None. A prefix is rejected. "f" is not "fit".

arguments.name: fixed_exponent, extra_sigfig
arguments.text: An exponent kept in the type. extra_sigfig True adds a star except when digits is set, which is an error. Only a real True counts.

translation.details: .data is the floats, with None for a missing value. .pillar is the formatted attribute, which is what vec_ptype_full returns. .abbr is vec_ptype_abbr.pillar_num. .classes starts with pillar_num. Decimal notation with a non-zero fixed exponent raises the installed text, including the spelling Incomatible. Zero and False do not. format.pillar_num and the numeric shaft are not implemented.
translation.value: A PillarNum. .data is a list of floats. .pillar and .abbr are strings.
translation.example:
from pillar.num import num

def show_num(value):
    bits = ["NA" if item is None else format(item, "g") for item in value.data]
    print(" ".join(bits))
    print(value.pillar)
    print(value.abbr)

show_num(num([1, 2.5, None]))
print()
show_num(num([1, 2], sigfig=4, label="kg"))
print()
show_num(num(1, digits=2, notation="sci"))
print()
show_num(num(1, notation="si", fixed_exponent=-3, scale=10, label="m"))
